edges.description: Chronic hepatocyte death and compensatory regeneration activate hepatic stellate cells.
A small portion of affected children develop AATD-associated neonatal cholestasis.
Hepatocellular carcinoma can occur in AATD-associated end-stage liver disease.
Stellate cell activation and collagen deposition produce hepatic fibrosis.
Progressive bridging fibrosis produces cirrhosis.
Alveolar wall destruction produces the panacinar emphysema phenotype.
Progressive emphysematous tissue destruction produces chronic obstructive pulmonary disease.
Neutrophilic inflammation and fat necrosis constitute the panniculitis lesion.

Emphysema is alveolar destruction, and the cited sentence names both the exposure and that outcome. Recorded as exacerbating rather than triggering because the destruction proceeds from the inherited antiprotease deficiency and smoking accelerates it, which is the word the source uses. The intervening step is the protease-antiprotease imbalance this entry models explicitly, so the intermediates are known rather than unknown.

Obesity and diabetes are recorded here as accelerants of the hepatic arm rather than the pulmonary one. Two limits are worth stating rather than leaving in the grade: the measurement is liver stiffness, a proxy for the fibrosis this node drives rather than a measure of stellate cell activation, and the finding is specific to heterozygous Pi*MZ adults rather than to the classic homozygous disease this entry mostly models.
